source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 6 (PDF 153-174, printed 150-171); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 6 (Emerging Technologies), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.
6.1 Definition and Overview of Emerging Technologies

blocks.prompt: 1 New tools, systems and methods that are currently being developed or have just started to be used are called:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: emerging technologies are new tools, systems and methods that are currently being developed or have just started to be used.

book_ref.quote: Emerging technologies are new tools, systems, and methods that are currently being developed

blocks.prompt: 2 Which two transformative technologies are the main subject of this chapter?
blocks.explanation: 6.1 (Introduction): the chapter explores Cloud Computing and Blockchain.

book_ref.quote: This chapter explores two of the most transformative technologies of our time

blocks.prompt: 3 Machines and software that can think and learn like humans are known as:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: AI refers to machines and software that can think and learn like humans, e.g. recognizing faces and understanding speech.

book_ref.quote: AI refers to machines and software that can think and learn like humans

blocks.prompt: 4 Smart assistants like Siri and self-driving cars are examples of the use of:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: AI is used in everything from smart assistants like Siri to self-driving cars.

book_ref.quote: It's used in everything from smart assistants like Siri to self-driving cars

blocks.prompt: 5 Google Drive, Dropbox and Amazon Web Services (AWS) are examples of:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: cloud computing lets people store and access data and applications over the internet; examples are Google Drive, Dropbox and AWS.

book_ref.quote: Examples include services like Google Drive, Dropbox, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)

blocks.prompt: 6 The technology best known for being behind cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin is:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: blockchain is best known as the technology behind cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin; it is also used in supply chains and contracts.

book_ref.quote: It's best known for being the technology behind cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin

blocks.prompt: 7 A smart thermostat that learns your schedule and adjusts the temperature of your home automatically is an example of:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: IoT connects everyday objects to the internet so they can send and receive data; the smart thermostat is the book's example.

book_ref.quote: a smart thermostat can learn your schedule and adjust the temperature

blocks.prompt: 8 Which technology adds digital elements to the real world using devices like smartphones or glasses?
blocks.explanation: 6.1: AR adds digital elements to the real world; VR instead creates a completely virtual environment.

book_ref.quote: AR adds digital elements to the real world using devices like smartphones or glasses

blocks.prompt: 9 Virtual Reality (VR) differs from AR because VR:

options.text: adds digital elements to the real world
creates a completely virtual environment used with special equipment
connects refrigerators and cars to the internet
uses living organisms to make products

blocks.explanation: 6.1: VR creates a completely virtual environment that you interact with using special equipment.

book_ref.quote: VR creates a completely virtual environment that you can interact with using special equipment

blocks.prompt: 10 5G is best described as:

options.text: a type of cloud deployment model
the next generation of wireless technology with faster speeds and more reliable connections

blocks.explanation: 6.1: 5G is the next generation of wireless technology, offering much faster internet speeds and more reliable connections.

book_ref.quote: 5G is the next generation of wireless technology

blocks.prompt: 11 Quantum computers process information using the principles of:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process information much faster than traditional computers.

book_ref.quote: Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process information

blocks.prompt: 12 Using living organisms like bacteria and plants to create new products or solve problems is called:
blocks.explanation: 6.1: biotechnology uses living organisms to develop new medicines, improve crops and create environmentally friendly materials.

book_ref.quote: Biotechnology involves using living organisms, like bacteria and plants

blocks.prompt: 13 Cloud computing gives access to computing resources like servers, storage and applications:
blocks.explanation: 6.2: cloud computing allows easy and convenient access to computing resources over the internet.

book_ref.quote: allows easy and convenient access to computing resources like servers, storage, and applications over the internet

blocks.prompt: 14 In cloud computing, how does a user normally pay?

options.text: a fixed price for buying the servers
for the provider's hardware in advance

blocks.explanation: 6.2: you can use as much or as little of the service as you need, and you only pay for what you use.

book_ref.quote: you only pay for what you use

blocks.prompt: 15 The book compares cloud computing to:

options.text: renting a supercomputer usable whenever needed, from anywhere

blocks.explanation: 6.2: cloud computing is like renting a supercomputer that you can use whenever you need it, from anywhere in the world.

book_ref.quote: It's like renting a supercomputer that you can use whenever you need it

blocks.prompt: 16 The technology that lets a single physical machine run multiple virtual machines is:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.1: virtualization allows a single physical machine to run multiple virtual machines.

book_ref.quote: Virtualization is a technology that allows a single physical machine to run multiple virtual machines

blocks.prompt: 17 With virtualization, each virtual computer inside a physical computer:

options.text: must share one operating system with the others
can run its own operating system and applications
needs its own physical hard disk

blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.1: each virtual computer can run its own operating system and applications as if it were an independent machine.

book_ref.quote: Each of these virtual computers can run its own operating system and applications

blocks.prompt: 18 Which of the following is NOT a benefit of virtualization given in the book?

options.text: It makes better use of the hardware
It allows easier management and flexibility

blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.1: virtualization makes better use of hardware, reduces costs and allows easier management and flexibility; it turns one computer into many.

book_ref.quote: This helps make better use of the hardware, reduces costs

blocks.prompt: 19 During Eid sales an online store gets a huge spike in traffic and adds more servers. This is an example of:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.2: scalability means you can add more resources (e.g. servers) when you need them.

book_ref.quote: Scalability means you can add more resources when you need them

blocks.prompt: 20 Elasticity differs from scalability because in elasticity the system:

options.text: adjusts resources automatically according to current demand
needs a manual setup for every change
runs on one physical server only

blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.2: elasticity takes scalability a step further by allowing the system to automatically adjust resources based on current demand.

book_ref.quote: Elasticity takes this a step further by allowing the system to automatically adjust

blocks.prompt: 21 In an elastic cloud system, what happens when the traffic decreases after a sale?

options.text: The number of servers is reduced so you do not pay for unneeded resources
The data is moved to a local computer

blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.2: when traffic decreases the system reduces the number of servers, so you are not paying for resources you don't need.

book_ref.quote: When the traffic decreases after the sale, the system can reduce the number of servers

blocks.prompt: 22 Turning on a tap to get water instead of digging a well first is the book's analogy for:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.3: on-demand access means using computing resources whenever needed without waiting for a long setup process, like turning on a tap.

book_ref.quote: This is like being able to turn on a tap to get water whenever you want

blocks.prompt: 23 A student suddenly needs extra storage for a school project and instantly rents it from a cloud provider. This shows:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.1.3: with on-demand access you can instantly rent additional storage from a cloud provider and start using it right away.

book_ref.quote: you can instantly rent additional storage from a cloud provider

blocks.prompt: 24 Into how many main types are cloud services typically categorized?
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2: cloud services are typically categorized into three main types: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

book_ref.quote: Cloud services are typically categorized into three main types

blocks.prompt: 25 Basic computing infrastructure such as servers, storage and networking on a pay-as-you-go basis is offered by:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.1: IaaS offers basic computing infrastructure such as servers, storage and networking on a pay-as-you-go basis.

book_ref.quote: IaaS offers basic computing infrastructure such as servers, storage, and networking

blocks.prompt: 26 In IaaS, users do NOT have control over:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.1: IaaS users control the operating systems, applications and storage, but not the underlying physical infrastructure.

book_ref.quote: Users have control over the operating systems, applications, and storage

blocks.prompt: 27 Renting virtual servers from AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Compute Engine to run your own applications is an example of:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.1: AWS lets users rent virtual servers; Microsoft Azure and Google Compute Engine are other popular IaaS providers.

book_ref.quote: Microsoft Azure and Google Compute Engine are other popular IaaS providers

blocks.prompt: 28 Besides infrastructure, PaaS includes:

options.text: middleware, development tools and management services

blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.2: PaaS includes infrastructure (servers, storage, networking), middleware, development tools and management services.

book_ref.quote: It includes infrastructure (servers, storage, and networking), middleware, development tools

blocks.prompt: 29 Google App Engine, Microsoft Azure App Services and Heroku are examples of:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.2: Google App Engine lets developers build and deploy applications; other PaaS examples are Microsoft Azure App Services and Heroku.

book_ref.quote: Other examples include Microsoft Azure App Services and Heroku

blocks.prompt: 30 In which service model do users simply subscribe and use software applications hosted and managed by the provider?
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3: SaaS provides access to software applications hosted and managed by the service provider; users subscribe and use it over the internet.

book_ref.quote: Users simply subscribe to the service and use it over the internet

blocks.prompt: 31 SaaS is convenient for end-users because it:

options.text: gives full control of physical servers
needs the user to install middleware
requires no hardware management or software updates

blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3: SaaS requires no hardware management or software updates from end-users.

book_ref.quote: This model is convenient for end-users as it requires no hardware management or software updates

blocks.prompt: 32 Google Workspace, which includes Gmail, Google Docs and Google Drive, was formerly called:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3: Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) is a SaaS example with Gmail, Google Docs and Google Drive.

book_ref.quote: Example: Google Workspace (formerly G Suite)

blocks.prompt: 33 Salesforce, one of the leading SaaS providers, is known for its:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3 (Did You Know?): Salesforce is known for its CRM platform; it helps businesses manage customer data, track sales and automate marketing.

book_ref.quote: known for its customer relationship management (CRM) platform

blocks.prompt: 34 According to the book, Salesforce is used by over:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3 (Did You Know?): over 150,000 companies use Salesforce to streamline business processes.

book_ref.quote: Over 150,000 companies use Salesforce

blocks.prompt: 35 Cloud computing services are priced:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.2.3 (Did You Know?): cloud services are priced based on usage; the pay-as-you-go model lets businesses scale resources to their needs.

book_ref.quote: Cloud computing services are priced based on usage

blocks.prompt: 36 What do cloud deployment models define?

options.text: how a block is linked to the previous block
how cloud services are made available and used
how virtual machines are switched off

blocks.explanation: 6.2.3: cloud deployment models define how cloud services are made available and used, with different levels of control, security and flexibility.

book_ref.quote: Cloud deployment models define how cloud services are made available and used

blocks.prompt: 37 Which of the following is NOT one of the main cloud deployment models named in the book?
blocks.explanation: 6.2.3: the main deployment models are Public, Private, Hybrid and Multi-Cloud. Serverless is an architecture (6.6.1.2), not a deployment model.

book_ref.quote: The main cloud deployment models are Public, Private, Hybrid, and Multi-Cloud

blocks.prompt: 38 A public cloud is managed by:

options.text: each user on their own computer

blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.1: a public cloud is offered over the internet, shared among multiple organizations and managed by a third-party cloud service provider.

book_ref.quote: It is managed by a third-party cloud service provider

blocks.prompt: 39 A private cloud can be hosted:

options.text: only by a third-party provider and shared with everyone
on-premises or by a third-party provider, but not shared with other organizations
only on the users' mobile phones

blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.2: a private cloud is used exclusively by one organization; it can be hosted on-premises or by a third-party provider but is not shared.

book_ref.quote: It can be hosted on-premises or by a third-party provider

blocks.prompt: 40 A large bank wants to handle sensitive customer data so that only the bank has access to it. The suitable model is:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.2: a large bank may use a private cloud for sensitive customer data; only the bank has access to it.

book_ref.quote: A large bank may use a private cloud to handle sensitive customer data securely

blocks.prompt: 41 In a hybrid cloud, during busy periods a company moves which of these to the public cloud?
blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.3: during busy periods less sensitive data and applications move to the public cloud while critical data stays secure in the private cloud.

book_ref.quote: they can move less sensitive data and applications to the public cloud

blocks.prompt: 42 A main reason for using a multi-cloud approach is to:

options.text: avoid dependency on a single provider
keep all data with one provider
remove the need for the internet

blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.4: multi-cloud uses services from different providers; it helps avoid dependency on a single provider and can enhance reliability and performance.

book_ref.quote: This model helps avoid dependency on a single provider

blocks.prompt: 43 A company uses Google Cloud Platform for data analytics, Microsoft Azure for enterprise applications and AWS for backup. This is:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.3.4: using services from different providers (GCP, Azure, AWS) is multi-cloud; if one provider has issues the company relies on the others.

book_ref.quote: A company might use Google Cloud Platform for its data analytics

blocks.prompt: 44 Which deployment model is cost-effective but less secure?
blocks.explanation: 6.2.4: public clouds are cost-effective but less secure; private clouds are more secure but expensive.

book_ref.quote: Public clouds are cost-effective but less secure

blocks.prompt: 45 According to the comparison of deployment models, resilience is provided by:
blocks.explanation: 6.2.4: hybrid clouds offer flexibility, while multi-clouds provide resilience.

book_ref.quote: while multi-clouds provide resilience

blocks.prompt: 46 Which statement about private clouds is correct according to the book?

options.text: They are cheaper but less secure
They are shared by many organizations
They are more secure but expensive

blocks.explanation: 6.2.4: private clouds are more secure but expensive.

book_ref.quote: Private clouds are more secure but expensive

blocks.prompt: 47 Cloud storage lets users save their data on:
blocks.explanation: 6.3.1.1: cloud storage saves data on remote servers rather than on local devices, so it can be accessed from anywhere and shared.

book_ref.quote: Cloud storage allows users to save data on remote servers rather than on local devices

blocks.prompt: 48 Businesses keep backups of their data in cloud storage mainly to keep it safe from:
blocks.explanation: 6.3.1.1: cloud backups keep data safe from local hardware failures or other issues.

book_ref.quote: ensuring it is safe from local hardware failures

blocks.prompt: 49 Cloudflare is an example of a:
blocks.explanation: 6.3.1.2: content delivery networks (CDNs) such as Cloudflare help deliver website content quickly.

book_ref.quote: Content delivery networks (CDNs) such as Cloudflare help deliver website content quickly

blocks.prompt: 50 A CDN delivers website content quickly by:

options.text: sending it from one central server only
caching it on servers close to the end-users

blocks.explanation: 6.3.1.2: CDNs deliver content quickly by caching it on servers close to the end-users.

book_ref.quote: by caching it on servers close to the end-users

blocks.prompt: 51 Google Cloud AI and AWS SageMaker are cloud-based platforms for:

options.text: building, training and deploying machine learning models

blocks.explanation: 6.3.1.3: Google Cloud AI and AWS SageMaker provide cloud platforms for building, training and deploying machine learning models.

book_ref.quote: Google Cloud AI and AWS SageMaker provide cloud-based platforms

blocks.prompt: 52 Storing sensitive data on remote servers introduces risks such as:
blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.1: security is a significant concern; storing sensitive data on remote servers introduces risks such as data breaches and loss.

book_ref.quote: Storing sensitive data on remote servers introduces risks such as data breaches and loss

blocks.prompt: 53 To mitigate security risks in the cloud, users should:

options.text: share their passwords with the provider
use encryption and strong authentication and regularly review security policies

blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.1: users should use encryption, strong authentication methods and regularly review their security policies.

book_ref.quote: users should use encryption, strong authentication methods

blocks.prompt: 54 Which practice is part of effective resource management in the cloud?

options.text: keeping all servers on at all times
monitoring resource usage and optimizing performance

blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.2: monitoring resource usage and optimizing performance help control costs and ensure efficient use of cloud resources.

book_ref.quote: such as monitoring resource usage and optimizing performance

blocks.prompt: 55 Why does cloud computing require careful financial management?

options.text: Users pay for what they use, and costs can quickly add up if not monitored
Users pay only once in a lifetime

blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.3: users pay for what they use, and costs can quickly add up if not monitored.

book_ref.quote: costs can quickly add up if not monitored

blocks.prompt: 56 Legal and regulatory requirements that cloud users must comply with:

options.text: can vary by region and industry

blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.4: organizations must comply with legal and regulatory requirements, which can vary by region and industry.

book_ref.quote: which can vary by region and industry

blocks.prompt: 57 Compliance in cloud computing means adhering to regulations related to:

options.text: data privacy, security and industry-specific standards

blocks.explanation: 6.3.2.4: organizations need to adhere to regulations related to data privacy, security and industry-specific standards.

book_ref.quote: regulations related to data privacy, security, and industry-specific standards

blocks.prompt: 58 Blockchain enables secure and transparent transactions through a:
blocks.explanation: 6.4: blockchain technology enables secure and transparent transactions through a distributed ledger system.

book_ref.quote: enables secure and transparent transactions through a distributed ledger system

blocks.prompt: 59 In the book's analogy, blockchain is like:

options.text: a paper kept by one person
a locked diary of one friend
a digital notebook that everyone in a group has a copy of

blocks.explanation: 6.4.1: blockchain is like a digital notebook shared with everyone in a group; every change is recorded in all the notebooks at the same time.

book_ref.quote: Blockchain is like a digital notebook that's shared with everyone in a group

blocks.prompt: 60 In blockchain, information is locked in place by a special kind of math called:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1: once something is written it is almost impossible to erase or change because it is protected by cryptography.

book_ref.quote: protected by a special kind of math called cryptography

blocks.prompt: 61 In the shared-notebook picture of decentralization, changes are made only when:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1: there is no single person or computer in charge; changes are only made when the majority agree.

book_ref.quote: changes are only made when the majority agree

blocks.prompt: 62 The feature of blockchain by which everyone can see what is recorded, making cheating hard, is:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1: transparency means everyone in the group can see what's written, so it is hard to cheat without others noticing.

book_ref.quote: Everyone in the group can see what's written in the notebook

blocks.prompt: 63 Because a blockchain is maintained by a network of nodes instead of a central authority, it:

options.text: reduces the risk of a single point of failure
can be edited by anyone alone
stops working if one node fails

blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.1: decentralization reduces the risk of a single point of failure and enhances security.

book_ref.quote: This decentralized nature reduces the risk of a single point of failure

blocks.prompt: 64 Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS) are examples of:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.1: blockchain networks use consensus mechanisms to agree on the validity of transactions; common ones are PoW and PoS.

book_ref.quote: Common consensus mechanisms include Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS)

blocks.prompt: 65 Before a new block is added to the chain, a consensus mechanism requires agreement of:

options.text: a sufficient majority of the network, not necessarily every node
only the user who sent the transaction

blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.1 (Book correction): consensus needs only a sufficient majority, e.g. the majority of computing power in PoW or a majority of the stake in PoS; a block is added even if some nodes are offline.

book_ref.quote: Consensus needs only a sufficient majority, not every node

blocks.prompt: 66 A computer that participates in the blockchain network and keeps a copy of the blockchain is called a:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.2: a node is a computer that participates in the blockchain network, keeps a copy of the blockchain and helps validate transactions and blocks.

book_ref.quote: A node is a computer that participates in the blockchain network

blocks.prompt: 67 The ledger in a blockchain is:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.2: the ledger is a digital record of all transactions, distributed across all nodes so everyone has the same information.

book_ref.quote: It is distributed across all nodes

blocks.prompt: 68 In a block, the reference to the previous block is called the:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.2: each block contains its own hash, a reference to the previous block (parent hash) and a list of transactions.

book_ref.quote: a reference to the previous block (parent hash)

blocks.prompt: 69 An individual entry in the blockchain that represents a transfer of assets or information between participants is a:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.2: a transaction is an individual entry in the blockchain representing a transfer of assets or information.

book_ref.quote: It represents the transfer of assets or information between participants

blocks.prompt: 70 The rules for how transactions are validated, how blocks are added and how consensus is achieved are defined by the:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.2: the blockchain protocol defines the rules and procedures for validation, adding blocks and consensus; it ensures integrity and security.

book_ref.quote: The blockchain protocol defines the rules and procedures

blocks.prompt: 71 In a peer-to-peer (P2P) network, each node can act as:

options.text: both a client and a server
neither a client nor a server

blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.3: each node in a P2P network can act as both a client and a server, making the network robust and decentralized.

book_ref.quote: Each node in the network can act as both a client and a server

blocks.prompt: 72 Downloading a file in a P2P file-sharing network is faster mainly because:

options.text: one central server sends the whole file
the file is stored only on one computer
multiple users can share parts of the file simultaneously

blocks.explanation: 6.4.1.3: users download directly from each other's computers, and multiple users can share parts of the file simultaneously.

book_ref.quote: multiple users can share parts of the file simultaneously

blocks.prompt: 73 Bitcoin and Ethereum are cryptocurrencies whose underlying technology is:
blocks.explanation: 6.4.2: blockchain is the underlying technology for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum.

book_ref.quote: Blockchain is the underlying technology for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum

blocks.prompt: 74 In supply chain management, blockchain is used to:

options.text: track and verify the movement of goods

blocks.explanation: 6.4.2: blockchain tracks and verifies the movement of goods; this transparency helps prevent fraud, reduce errors and ensure authenticity.

book_ref.quote: Blockchain can be used to track and verify the movement of goods

blocks.prompt: 75 Using blockchain in voting systems helps mainly by:

options.text: making votes secret from the counting system
recording and counting votes accurately and reducing the risk of election fraud
removing the need to count votes

blocks.explanation: 6.4.2: blockchain can create secure and transparent voting systems, ensuring votes are accurately recorded and counted and reducing election fraud.

book_ref.quote: reducing the risk of election fraud

blocks.prompt: 76 In healthcare, blockchain can:

options.text: securely store patient records and allow access only to authorised individuals

blocks.explanation: 6.4.2: in healthcare, blockchain can securely store patient records and ensure only authorised individuals access sensitive information.

book_ref.quote: blockchain can securely store patient records

blocks.prompt: 77 Cryptocurrencies are digital currencies that work:

options.text: without traditional banks, allowing direct transactions between people

blocks.explanation: 6.4.3: cryptocurrencies are digital currencies that work without traditional banks, allowing direct transactions between people worldwide.

book_ref.quote: Cryptocurrencies are digital currencies that work without traditional banks

blocks.prompt: 78 According to the book, cryptocurrencies help people who do not have access to traditional banking services to:

options.text: take part in the global economy

blocks.explanation: 6.4.3.1: cryptocurrencies let people send money quickly and cheaply across borders and help the unbanked take part in the global economy.

book_ref.quote: They also help people who don't have access to traditional banking services

blocks.prompt: 79 The book's example of a smart contract in insurance automatically pays out when:

options.text: a flight is delayed, based on pre-set conditions

blocks.explanation: 6.4.3.2: an insurance smart contract can automatically pay out if a flight is delayed, based on pre-set conditions.

book_ref.quote: an insurance smart contract can automatically pay out if a flight is delayed

blocks.prompt: 80 Which platform is named in the book for creating decentralized applications (DApps) using smart contracts?
blocks.explanation: 6.4.3.2: platforms like Ethereum enable developers to create DApps using smart contracts.

book_ref.quote: Platforms like Ethereum enable developers to create decentralized applications (DApps)

blocks.prompt: 81 Which is a challenge of smart contracts mentioned in the book?

options.text: the need for error-free code and legal systems to resolve disputes

blocks.explanation: 6.4.3.2: smart contracts are transparent and secure, but they need error-free code and legal systems to resolve disputes.

book_ref.quote: such as the need for error-free code and legal systems

blocks.prompt: 82 Because smart contracts run on blockchain technology, they:

options.text: can be changed by one party
remove the need for intermediaries and reduce errors and fraud

blocks.explanation: 6.4.3.2: smart contracts run on blockchain, removing the need for intermediaries and reducing the risk of errors and fraud.

book_ref.quote: removing the need for intermediaries and reducing the risk of errors and fraud

blocks.prompt: 83 In section 6.5, blockchain is described as a digital notebook that:

options.text: everyone can see, but no one can change
is kept on a single computer

blocks.explanation: 6.5: blockchain is like a digital notebook that everyone can see, but no one can change.

book_ref.quote: It's like a digital notebook that everyone can see, but no one can change

blocks.prompt: 84 Recording every step of a product's journey on a decentralized ledger mainly helps in:

options.text: verifying authenticity, ensuring quality and finding the source of issues

blocks.explanation: 6.5.1: traceability helps in verifying the authenticity of products, ensuring quality and identifying the source of any issues.

book_ref.quote: This traceability helps in verifying the authenticity of products

blocks.prompt: 85 Figure 6.3 of the chapter shows blockchain tracking the origin of:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.1: Figure 6.3 shows tracking the origin of chocolate using blockchain.

book_ref.quote: Tracking the origin of chocolate using blockchain

blocks.prompt: 86 When a supplier delivers raw materials to a manufacturer in a blockchain-tracked supply chain:

options.text: no record is kept until the sale
the customer must phone the supplier
a record is created and added to the blockchain

blocks.explanation: 6.5.1: a record is created and added to the blockchain at each stage, giving a verifiable history that the customer can access.

book_ref.quote: a record is created and added to the blockchain

blocks.prompt: 87 Artists who sell digital art using blockchain prove that a piece is the original by its:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.1 (Did You Know?): each piece of digital art sold on blockchain has a unique digital signature proving it is the original.

book_ref.quote: Each piece of art has a unique digital signature

blocks.prompt: 88 Sending money abroad is often slow and expensive. Blockchain in financial services makes it:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.2: banks and financial services use blockchain to make transactions faster and safer; sending money abroad becomes quicker and cheaper.

book_ref.quote: Blockchain makes it quicker and cheaper

blocks.prompt: 89 In blockchain-based verification of academic certificates, who records the certificate details on the decentralized ledger?
blocks.explanation: 6.5.2 (Class Activity): the issuing authority records certificate details on a decentralized ledger; anyone can then verify them quickly and securely.

book_ref.quote: the issuing authority records the certificate details on a decentralized ledger

blocks.prompt: 90 In the secure-letter example, placing the letter in a special envelope that only your friend can open stands for:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.3: sealing the letter is like encryption, where data is turned into a code only the intended recipient (with the right key) can understand.

book_ref.quote: Sealing the Letter (Encryption)

blocks.prompt: 91 In the secure-letter example, signing the envelope with your unique signature stands for:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.3: the digital signature ensures that the data comes from a legitimate source and hasn't been tampered with.

book_ref.quote: Signing the Letter (Digital Signature)

blocks.prompt: 92 Sending copies of the letter through different trusted services to several places stands for:
blocks.explanation: 6.5.3: decentralization stores data across multiple computers (nodes), so even if one is compromised the data remains safe.

book_ref.quote: Multiple Copies of the Letter (Decentralization)

blocks.prompt: 93 Which part of blockchain security records every action so that any attempt to tamper with data is easily detected?
blocks.explanation: 6.5.3: the blockchain network records every action, so any attempt to tamper with the data is easily detected.

book_ref.quote: The Blockchain Network records every action

blocks.prompt: 94 Edge computing processes data:

options.text: only after storing it on paper
only on the customer's bank server
near the data source, at the edge of the network
